```{r exampledata}

library(psych)
data(bfi)            ## fresh load each time (no mistake RE-recodes)

bfi$A1 <- 7-bfi$A1   ## Item recodes

bfi$C4 <- 7-bfi$C4
bfi$C5 <- 7-bfi$C5

bfi$E1 <- 7-bfi$E1
bfi$E2 <- 7-bfi$E2

bfi$O2 <- 7-bfi$O2
bfi$O5 <- 7-bfi$O5


respondent <- bfi[2800,]    ## isolating 1 respondent, change to any number (1-2800) to run a report on a different individual
norms      <- bfi[-2800,]

respondent[29] <- "Nörm N Nörmman"
colnames(respondent)[29] <- "name"

```

```{r norms}

agree_norm <- rowMeans(norms[1:5], na.rm=TRUE) 
cons_norm  <- rowMeans(norms[6:10], na.rm=TRUE)
extra_norm <- rowMeans(norms[11:15], na.rm=TRUE)
neuro_norm <- rowMeans(norms[16:20], na.rm=TRUE)
open_norm  <- rowMeans(norms[21:25], na.rm=TRUE)

agree_mean <- mean(agree_norm, na.rm = TRUE)
agree_sd   <- sd(agree_norm, na.rm = TRUE)

cons_mean  <- mean(cons_norm, na.rm = TRUE)
cons_sd    <- sd(cons_norm, na.rm = TRUE)

extra_mean <- mean(extra_norm, na.rm = TRUE)
extra_sd   <- sd(extra_norm, na.rm = TRUE)

neuro_mean <- mean(neuro_norm, na.rm = TRUE)
neuro_sd   <- sd(neuro_norm, na.rm = TRUE)

open_mean  <- mean(open_norm, na.rm = TRUE)
open_sd    <- sd(open_norm, na.rm = TRUE)

```

```{r scoring}

## focal person's scores

agree <- rowMeans(respondent[1:5], na.rm=TRUE) 
cons  <- rowMeans(respondent[6:10], na.rm=TRUE)
extra <- rowMeans(respondent[11:15], na.rm=TRUE)
neuro <- rowMeans(respondent[16:20], na.rm=TRUE)
open  <- rowMeans(respondent[21:25], na.rm=TRUE)

## Scale scores (μ=100, σ=15)

agree_ss <- round(((((agree-agree_mean)/agree_sd)*15)+100),0)
cons_ss  <- round(((((cons-cons_mean)/cons_sd)*15)+100),0)
extra_ss <- round(((((extra-extra_mean)/extra_sd)*15)+100),0)
neuro_ss <- round(((((neuro-neuro_mean)/neuro_sd)*15)+100),0)
open_ss  <- round(((((open-open_mean)/open_sd)*15)+100),0)

scores <- rbind(agree_ss, cons_ss, extra_ss, neuro_ss, open_ss)
dimension <- c("Agreeableness", 
               "Conscientiousness", 
               "Extraversion",
               "Neuroticism",
               "Openness")
toplot <- as.data.frame(cbind(dimension, scores))
colnames(toplot)[2] <- "Standard Score"

toplot$`Standard Score` <- as.numeric(as.character(toplot$`Standard Score`))

```

\newpage

## Assessment information

The BFI consists of 25 personality items and 3 demographics (gender, education, and age). Responses to the 25 personality items determine an individuals standing along 5 personality dimensions:

+ **Extraversion** -- an orientation of interest and energies ranging from the outer world of people and things to the inner world of subjective experience 
+ **Conscientiousness** -- a tendency to be organized, responsible, and hardworking/industrious 
+ **Agreeableness** -- tendency to act in a cooperative, unselfish manner 
+ Openness to experience (**Openness**) -- tendency to be open to new aesthetic, cultural, or intellectual experiences
+ **Neuroticism** -- chronic levels of emotional instability and proneness to psychological distress

## Results summary for `r respondent$name`:

There were `r sum(is.na(respondent[1:25]))` missing responses across 25 personality item administrations.

When compared against responses of `r nrow(norms)` other individuals, `r respondent$name`'s personality profile can be extracted from @fig-radarplot and @fig-barplot.

```{r}
#| label: fig-radarplot
#| fig-cap: "Standard score radar plot across 5 dimensions"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 6

library(fmsb)

data_for_radar <- data.frame(
  row.names = c("Max", "Min", "Your Profile"),   # row names important!
  Agreeableness     = c(140, 60, toplot$`Standard Score`[toplot$dimension == "Agreeableness"]),
  Conscientiousness = c(140, 60, toplot$`Standard Score`[toplot$dimension == "Conscientiousness"]),
  Extraversion      = c(140, 60, toplot$`Standard Score`[toplot$dimension == "Extraversion"]),
  Neuroticism       = c(140, 60, toplot$`Standard Score`[toplot$dimension == "Neuroticism"]),
  Openness          = c(140, 60, toplot$`Standard Score`[toplot$dimension == "Openness"])
)

# Plot – solid fill, customizable
radarchart(
  data_for_radar,
  axistype           = 1,                # 1 = show axis values
  pcol               = "steelblue",      # line color
  pfcol              = scales::alpha("steelblue", 0.4),  # fill color + alpha
  plwd               = 2,                # line width
  cglcol             = "grey80",         # grid color
  cglty              = 1,                # grid line type
  axislabcol         = "grey50",         # axis label color
  caxislabels        = seq(60, 140, 20), # radial labels (customize breaks)
  vlcex              = 0.9              # label size
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-barplot
#| fig-cap: "Standard score dotplot across 5 dimensions"

## Redundant with radar plot - simply here as an example of another plot type

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(toplot, aes(x = reorder(dimension, `Standard Score`), y=`Standard Score`)) +
  geom_segment( aes(y=0, yend=`Standard Score`)) +
  geom_point(size=9.5, color="#0000d1", alpha=.8) +      ## adding border
  geom_point(size=8, color="#6baed6", alpha=.8) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = `Standard Score`), color = "black", size = 3.5) +
  labs(x="",y="") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(80, 100, 120), labels = c("low", "average", "high")) +
  theme(legend.position="none", text=element_text(family="Times")) +
  coord_flip(ylim=c(60,140))
```

```{r}
## Qualitative statements of lower, average or above
## Can be expanded for further text specification
agreereport <- NULL

agreereport[agree_ss == 100] <- "average" 
agreereport[agree_ss > 100] <- "above average"
agreereport[agree_ss < 100] <- "below average"

consreport <- NULL

consreport[cons_ss == 100] <- "average" 
consreport[cons_ss > 100] <- "above average"
consreport[cons_ss < 100] <- "below average"

extrareport[extra_ss == 100] <- "average" 
extrareport[extra_ss > 100] <- "above average"

```


## Interpretation and Summary

Scores above 100 indicate greater than average whereas scores below 100 indicate less than average. 

`r respondent$name` scored `r agreereport` on Agreeableness, `r consreport` on Conscientiousness, `r extrareport` on Extraversion, `r neuroreport` on Neuroticism, and `r openreport` on Openness.

# Appendix

Reported scores should be interpreted relative to an average of 100 and standard deviation of 15. These values are extracted from a normative comparison group of `r nrow(norms)` men and women between the ages of `r min(norms$age)` and `r max(norms$age)` (average age = `r round(mean(norms$age),2)`, standard deviation = `r round(sd(norms$age),2)`, see @fig-norms).

```{r}
#| label: fig-norms
#| fig-cap: "Normative group age and gender distributions"

library(dplyr)

norms$gender <- ifelse(norms$gender < 1.2, "Male", "Female")

means <- norms %>%
  group_by(gender) %>%
  summarise(mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(norms, aes(x = age, fill = gender)) +
  geom_histogram(position = "dodge",  ## or "identity"
    alpha = 0.7, 
    color = "#333333",   ## border
    bins = 30                
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    data = means,
    aes(xintercept = mean_age, color = gender),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1
  )

```

The raw score values for the `r nrow(norms)` individuals can be found in @tbl-norms.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-norms
#| fig-cap: "Normative group raw scores on personality dimensions"

library(kableExtra)

rawscores <- data.frame(t(
  data.frame(
    c(round(agree_mean,2), round(agree_sd,2)),
    c(round(cons_mean,2), round(cons_sd,2)),
    c(round(extra_mean,2), round(extra_sd,2)),
    c(round(neuro_mean,2), round(neuro_sd,2)),
    c(round(open_mean,2), round(open_sd,2))
  )
))

row.names(rawscores) <- c("Agreeableness", "Conscientiousness", "Extraversion", "Neuroticism", "Openness")
colnames(rawscores) <- c("mean", "sd")

rawscores |>
  kbl(format="latex", booktabs=TRUE) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = "striped")

```
